title: Platform systems & services: playbook, how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Sophie Chen
body:
Summary: This document consolidates the platform engineering team’s authoritative guidance for systems & services ownership, common how-tos, dashboards & alerts standards, operational runbooks, retrospective practices, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended for oncall engineers, service owners, SREs, and product partners who depend on the Redwood inference platform runtime and supporting services.

Scope: Covers core platform systems (runtime control plane, routing, caching, autoscaler, provisioning, observability stack), internal services (billing-bridge, quota-service, telemetry-ingest), dashboards & alerts conventions, runbooks for P0/P1 incidents, quarterly roadmap priorities, and the team wiki structure. Does NOT contain customer-specific runbooks or legal/compliance artifacts (see security-and-compliance space).

Ownership and contacts:
- Platform team lead: Sophie Chen (author) — primary program owner.
- Oncall rotation: platform-sre@redwood.com (follow rota in PagerDuty).
- Escalation matrix: oncall -> platform-ops -> head of eng (pages/contact list in team wiki).
- Component owners: see appendix A (Service Inventory).

Quick links:
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.com/services/platform
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/platform-overview
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-runbook-roadmap-2026
- Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Service inventory (summary table):
| Service | Primary owner | SLA/SLO | Critical alerts | Notes |
| Runtime API (runtime-control) | Marco Diaz | 99.95% p99 latency < 250ms | runtime-5xx-rate, runtime-kv-cache-miss | Core inference path |
| Autoscaler | Aisha Patel | 99.9% scale-up within 90s | autoscaler-queue-growth, autoscaler-failed-calls | Responsible for Dedicated pools |
| Quota & Billing bridge | Ravi Kumar | N/A (non-customer facing) | billing-error-rate, quota-sync-latency | Integrates with billing pipeline |
| Telemetry-ingest | Devina Singh | 99.9% availability | telemetry-lag, kafka-consumer-error | Backpressure can impact dashboards |

Standards: dashboards & alerts
- Dashboard naming: All dashboards live under Grafana folder 'Platform / <component>'. Panel names: <component> - <metric> - <aggregation>.
- Dashboard minimums for a service:
  1) Health / error rate (5m and 1h views)
  2) Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) by route
  3) Capacity / utilization (GPU/CPU/memory/queue length)
  4) Throughput (requests/s, tokens/s)
  5) Dependency map (upstream/downstream status)
- Alert naming convention: <severity>::<component>::<short-metric> (e.g., P0::runtime::5xx-rate).
- Alert severity definitions (platform policy):
  - P0: user-visible outage or severe data loss risk. PagerDuty escalation. Target MTTA < 10m.
  - P1: degraded customer experience (latency or partial capacity loss). PagerDuty notify; page if sustained > 10m.
  - P2: operational issue with workarounds; handled during business hours.
- Alert thresholds examples (baseline):
  - P0 runtime-5xx-rate > 1% sustained for 5m OR p99 latency > 1.5s for 5m.
  - P1 autoscaler-queue-growth rate > 100% for 10m OR failed scale actions > 5 per 10m.
  - P1 telemetry-lag > 2m for 15m.

Dashboards: recommended panels (copy/paste JSON snippets in Grafana folder)
- Platform overview (single pane): global qps, error rate, p99 latency, capacity headroom.
- Runtime detail: per-model latency heatmap, kv-cache hit rate, active KV sessions.
- Autoscaler detail: scale events timeline, queue length histogram, failed actions.
- Billing bridge: sync lag, queued invoices, retry rates.

How-tos (common operational procedures)
1) Accessing production Grafana and finding the right panel:
   - Login via SSO -> Grafana Home -> Folder: Platform -> <component> -> Use time-range last 1h then 24h.
2) Running a controlled rollout for config changes (e.g., batching config):
   - Create draft config in repo: infra/feature-flags/<change>.yaml.
   - Submit PR with test plan and canary strategy.
   - Canary: deploy to 5% runtime nodes, monitor runtime-5xx-rate and p99 latency for 30m.
   - If stable, increase incrementally (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 15–30m observation windows.
   - If regressions appear, flip flag to previous version and notify stakeholders.
3) Performing capacity scale exercises (game-day):
   - Pre-checks: ensure autoscaler health, quota-service responsive, and telemetry-lag < 30s.
   - Execute synthetic load (tools: loadgen/runtime-load) to target QPS.
   - Validate scale-up completed within SLO and no sustained p99 > 1s.

Runbooks (P0 and P1 playbooks)
- P0: Total runtime outage (no responses for hosted API)
  1) Acknowledge PagerDuty and post incident channel: #incidents-platform.
  2) Run quick health checks: `kubectl get pods -n runtime` and `curl -sS https://runtime-health.internal/health`.
  3) Check Grafana: errors panel, upstream dependencies (kafka, datastore).
  4) If root cause is resource exhaustion: increase equiv pods via `kubectl scale` or trigger emergency autoscaler override (ops CLI `ops autoscaler override --pool runtime --count <n>`).
  5) If build or deploy caused issue: rollback to last stable image (ops deploy rollback runtime).
  6) Notify customers via Status Page and update every 30 minutes until resolution.
  7) Postmortem: create incident doc in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems within 72 hours.
- P1: Degraded latency or partial capacity loss
  1) Triage by owner, validate affected routes, identify start time and recent changes.
  2) If autoscaler misbehaving, check event logs and consider manual scale-up for impacted pools.
  3) If specific model causing hotspot, route traffic away using routing rules (console or ops CLI).
  4) Apply temporary rate-limiting or shed non-critical workloads.
  5) Monitor and escalate to P0 if user impact widens.

Retrospective & post-incident process
- Timeline:
  1) Immediate remediation and status updates.
  2) 24–72 hour initial incident write-up (facts, timeline, impact).
  3) Triage meeting within 5 business days.
  4) Blameless postmortem with action items, owners, and due dates.
- Template items: summary, timeline, impact (customers, revenue, SLO), root cause, contributing factors, action items (with owner and ETA), follow-ups.
- Action tracking: publish actions in retro board and create Jira tickets tagged `platform-incident-action`.

Roadmap (next 3 quarters)
- Q3 2026:
  - Autoscaler hardening: reduce scale-up time from 90s -> 45s; implement backpressure-aware policies.
  - Observability: rollout model-level tracing and end-to-end request ids.
  - Runbooks: consolidate component runbooks and add playbook tests to CI.
- Q4 2026:
  - Dedicated capacity improvements: improve pool rebalancing and burst capacity limits.
  - Cost optimization: caching policy A/B tests and intelligent quantization recommendations integration.
- Q1 2027:
  - Private deployments: standardize on onprem packaging and automated upgrade path.
  - Reliability: target p99 latency reduction by 20% across common workloads.

Team wiki structure (recommended pages)
- Team home: mission, oncall rota, working agreements.
- Systems index: short entries for each service with owner, last runbook update date, and direct Grafana links.
- How-tos & runbooks: canonical procedures, CLI references, and game-day exercises.
- Retrospectives: chronological list of postmortems and action trackers.

Appendix A: Component owner (short list)
- runtime-control: Marco Diaz (marco.diaz@redwood.com)
- autoscaler: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.com)
- quota-service: Ravi Kumar (ravi.kumar@redwood.com)
- telemetry-ingest: Devina Singh (devina.singh@redwood.com)

Appendix B: Operational checklists (copyable)
- Pre-deploy checklist:
  - Run unit and integration tests (CI green).
  - Confirm canary config present and monitoring dashboards linked in PR.
  - Notify oncall for major releases.

Revision history:
- 2026-07-15: Created by Sophie Chen.
- 2026-08-02: Updated autoscaler SLO and added dashboard naming conventions (reviewers: Marco Diaz, Aisha Patel, Ravi Kumar).

If something is missing or you need a deeper runbook for a particular service, file a request in the platform team backlog with label `platform-runbook-request`.
